findings.title: `dhf.sessions` is fully mutable except by convention, so attribution and epoch metadata can be rewritten after the fact
findings.evidence: `-- dhf.sessions.ended_at is UPDATE-able (that's how we close sessions), so no trigger.` and the table includes mutable audit fields such as `user_identity`, `workstation_id`, `sw_version`, `addin_version`, `orchestrator_version`, `protocol_version`, `addin_session_id`, `started_at`.
findings.problem: The spec permits unrestricted UPDATEs to every column in `dhf.sessions`, not just `ended_at`. Those fields are not covered by the entry hash chain, so user identity, workstation identity, version provenance, and session epoch can be altered without hash validation detecting it.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks the audit claims of the ledger. A rewritten session row can change who performed the actions, where they occurred, and which `addin_session_id` the entries belong to, while all entry hashes still validate.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a DB trigger that allows only the intended `ended_at` transition and rejects changes to all other `dhf.sessions` columns. If session metadata is intended to be auditable, hash or otherwise integrity-protect it as part of session creation.

findings.title: The timestamp canonicalization rule is contradicted by the append code, which hashes a normalized timestamp but appears to insert the raw timestamp
findings.evidence: Section 4.1: `The same normalized string MUST be used for both the INSERT parameter and the hash input.` Section 7: `Timestamp = turn.Timestamp` and `CanonicalTimestamp = canonicalTimestamp // Used for hash input`.
findings.problem: The code path shown computes a canonical UTC microsecond string for hashing, but the inserted row still uses `turn.Timestamp`. If the input has a non-UTC offset or more than microsecond precision, Postgres will store a value that is not byte-equivalent to the value hashed.
findings.why_it_matters: Shallow validation can fail on legitimate rows, or hash stability can depend on implicit Postgres normalization rather than the stated canonicalization rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Normalize and truncate the timestamp once, then use that normalized value for both the DB insert and the hash input. Do not insert the raw `turn.Timestamp` if the hash was computed from a different representation.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown closes the session, which conflicts with the stated rule that reconnect with the same `AddinSessionId` resumes the prior session
findings.evidence: `SDR-04-005: Same-AddinSessionId reconnect resumes the prior session.` Section 6.2: `ShutdownAsync calls DhfSessionManager.CloseSessionAsync(sessionId) which sets ended_at = NOW().`
findings.problem: If the orchestrator restarts cleanly while the add-in remains loaded, the existing session is explicitly closed. The next `AddinReadyMessage` with the same `AddinSessionId` will open a new session, not resume the old one.
findings.why_it_matters: Session boundaries become dependent on orchestrator process lifecycle, not only on add-in epoch. That changes chain semantics and undermines the claimed distinction between add-in reload and transient orchestrator disconnect.
findings.proposed_fix: Either keep sessions open across orchestrator restarts until a new `AddinSessionId` is observed, or explicitly redefine graceful shutdown as a session-ending event and update SDR-04-005, acceptance criteria, and downstream readers accordingly.

findings.title: Integrity-event deduplication is defined as `same eventType on the same entry`, which is too coarse to preserve distinct failures
findings.evidence: `Deep validation deduplicates before writing: it checks for an existing integrity_event decoration of the same eventType on the same entry before inserting a new one. If an identical event already exists, no new row is written.`
findings.problem: `same eventType` is not the same as `identical event`. Multiple different failures on one entry can share the same `eventType` but differ in affected artifact, path, expected hash, or actual hash.
findings.why_it_matters: Deep validation can suppress new integrity evidence and make the stored event history incomplete or misleading.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a concrete dedup fingerprint that includes `eventType` plus the affected field/artifact and relevant values (for example path plus expected/actual hash), and align the wording with that exact rule.

top_3_must_fix: Restrict `dhf.sessions` updates so only `ended_at` can change; all other session metadata is currently mutable and unhashed.
Use the same normalized UTC microsecond timestamp for both INSERT and hash computation; the current spec/code example shows different values.
Resolve the contradiction between `SDR-04-005` resume semantics and `Close on Shutdown`; define whether graceful orchestrator restart splits or resumes a DHF session.
